Subject: Re: Live chat SSE surge: increased p99 disconnects & errors

Hi Rishi,

We're seeing a large spike in streaming chat disconnects and p99 latency starting ~07:45 UTC this morning during our peak window. Affected clients are on the SSE endpoint (v1/stream/chat). Symptoms: intermittent 502/504 and socket resets, multiple reconnects, and a 7-12s p99 for token streaming. This is impacting live patient chat sessions.

Quick details:
- First observed: 2027-04-11 07:45:13 UTC
- Example request IDs: req-8fa3c2, req-8fa3d9 (included in attached request_samples.log)
- Topline metric: p99 from baseline ~1.2s -> 9.2s at peak
- We also saw elevated 429s as clients retried aggressively

I've attached a small screenshot of the metric (boxline_spike_utc0745.png) and a trimmed ndjson dump of failing SSE frames (sse_dump_0745.ndjson). Can you confirm if this is a known degradation on the hosted API and provide an ETA? We're starting to route traffic to a fallback but will need a durable fix.

Appreciate any visibility you can provide; this is high-severity for us.

Thanks,
Alex Cho
CTO, Boxline Health

Subject: Re: Live chat SSE surge: increased p99 disconnects & errors

Status update (investigation + mitigation applied):

Summary: At ~09:00 UTC we observed worker queue depth spikes on the SSE streaming pool for v1/stream/chat correlated with a burst of large-context requests from a single Boxline shard. Root cause appears to be a combination of: aggressive client reconnects + longer-than-expected KV cache misses causing per-request regeneration. The streaming worker pool experienced queue head-of-line blocking under heavy retry patterns.

Actions taken (12:00 UTC):
- Enabled emergency routing for Boxline namespace to a reserved dedicated pool (reduced contention).
- Increased autoscaler headroom to allow +30% worker capacity for SSE routes.
- Temporarily enabled aggressive prefix KV caching and disabled a non-critical post-processing hook that amplified tail latency.
- For a subset of clients we enabled short-poll fallback to avoid persistent SSE handshakes.

Result: p99 dropped from ~9.2s at peak to ~1.4s within 20 minutes after routing change. Error rates for the SSE route dropped ~78%. We've kept the emergency routing active while we gather detailed traces.

Next steps:
- Collect full flame graphs and kernel perf traces (SUP-3945).
- Prepare an RCA and a tracked remediation plan with timeline (target: preliminary RCA within 48 hours).
- Consider a long-term mitigation: more conservative reconnect guidance, better client-side jitter, and a guardrail on per-shard request rate.

I'll attach log snippets to the Jira ticket. Let me know if Boxline needs an immediate customer-facing summary.

—Dylan Brooks
SRE, Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com
